name: Baalis
overview: Baalis was a male monarch known as the king of the sons of Ammon, as recorded in Jeremiah 40:14. Beyond his royal status, Scripture provides no additional personal details about his tribe or background. His role is specifically identified within the context of Ammonite leadership during a turbulent period in Israel's history.
namesAndTitles: The name Baalis likely means 'son of delight' or relates to 'Baals,' reflecting common ancient Near Eastern naming patterns. His title, 'king of the sons of Ammon,' clearly designates his authority over the Ammonite people, emphasizing his political and national leadership role as noted in Jeremiah 40:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Baalis beyond his position as king of the sons of Ammon. No additional familial connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Baalis holds significance as a political figure during the prophetic era of Jeremiah, representing the Ammonite kingdom's leadership. His mention in Jeremiah 40:14 situates him in the broader narrative of Israel's neighbors and their interactions during a critical period of covenantal challenges and divine judgment. Though details are sparse, his kingship reflects the geopolitical realities surrounding Israel and Judah in the Old Testament.
